quiz.question_id: Dalam table-driven test, mengapa test cases dikumpulkan dalam slice of struct?
quiz.question_en: In a table-driven test, why are test cases collected in a slice of structs?
options_id: Agar satu loop bisa menguji banyak kasus tanpa menduplikasi assertion logic
options_en: So one loop can test many cases without duplicating assertion logic
So all tests become parallel automatically
So `testing.T` is no longer needed
So the compiler generates mocks

quiz.question_en: What is the main role of `tt.name` in `t.Run(tt.name, ...)`?
options_id: Memberi nama subtest agar output jelas dan bisa difilter
options_en: It chooses the target package
It names the subtest so output is clear and filterable
It sets the number of benchmark iterations
It sets a timeout per subtest

quiz.question_id: Perintah mana yang paling sesuai untuk hanya menjalankan subtest `positive numbers` di `TestAdd` menurut pola lesson?
quiz.question_en: Which command best matches the lesson for running only the `positive numbers` subtest inside `TestAdd`?
options_en: `go test -run TestAdd/positive_numbers`
`go test -subtest positive numbers`
`go test TestAdd.positive numbers`
`go test -run positive numbers/TestAdd`

quiz.question_id: Mengapa pemeriksaan `(err != nil) != tt.wantErr` dilakukan sebelum membandingkan `got`?
quiz.question_en: Why is `(err != nil) != tt.wantErr` checked before comparing `got`?
options_id: Karena nilai hasil baru bermakna jika status error sudah sesuai ekspektasi
options_en: Because Go requires it for subtests
Because the returned value is only meaningful once the error state matches expectations
So `t.Run` can return a bool
Because `wantErr` must always be false

quiz.question_id: Mengapa contoh `TestDivide` langsung `return` setelah menemukan mismatch pada error state?
quiz.question_en: Why does the sample `TestDivide` immediately `return` after finding an error-state mismatch?
options_id: Agar pemeriksaan nilai tidak memakai hasil yang tidak relevan atau belum valid
options_en: So the subtest is skipped
So the outer loop stops entirely
So value checks do not use a result that is irrelevant or not valid yet
Because `t.Errorf` would panic without `return`

quiz.question_id: Manakah set field yang paling idiomatis untuk struct test case menurut lesson?
quiz.question_en: Which set of fields is most idiomatic for the test case struct according to the lesson?
options_en: `first`, `second`, `answer`, `flag`
`input`, `output`, `exception`
`name`, input data, `want`, and if needed `wantErr`
`caseID`, `state`, `message`, `done`

quiz.question_id: Mengapa penggunaan nama variabel loop `tt` dianggap idiomatis?
quiz.question_en: Why is the loop variable name `tt` considered idiomatic?
options_id: Karena itu konvensi ringkas yang membuat pattern table-driven familiar untuk dibaca
Karena hanya `tt` yang bisa di-capture oleh closure
options_en: Because `tt` is a Go keyword
Because it is a compact convention that makes the table-driven pattern familiar to read
Because only `tt` can be captured by a closure
Because the `testing` package looks for that name

quiz.question_id: Kasus mana yang paling cocok disebut edge case berdasarkan saran lesson?
quiz.question_en: Which set best matches the edge cases suggested by the lesson?
options_id: Zero, nilai negatif, string kosong, atau overflow
options_en: Only the most common inputs
Zero, negative values, empty strings, or overflow
Only inputs that pass validation
Cases that require a real database

quiz.question_id: Apa keuntungan tambahan subtest selain organisasi kode?
quiz.question_en: What additional benefit do subtests provide beyond code organization?
options_id: Setiap subtest punya `*testing.T` sendiri dan muncul terpisah di output verbose
Setiap subtest selalu berjalan di process terpisah
options_en: Each subtest has its own `*testing.T` and appears separately in verbose output
Each subtest always runs in a separate process
Each subtest automatically uses mocks
Subtests remove the need for assertions

quiz.question_id: Jika `tt.wantErr` bernilai true, pola lesson memperlakukan field `want` bagaimana?
quiz.question_en: If `tt.wantErr` is true, how does the lesson's pattern treat the `want` field?
options_id: Tidak relevan untuk assertion nilai sampai error expectation sudah lolos
options_en: It still must be compared with `got`
It must be set to `-1`
It is not relevant for value assertions until the error expectation has passed
It is used to store the error message
